Method of Attack: Takes over users' browsers and uses JavaScript code to perform click-jacking
Gives Facebook likes to content from a central command and control server
Packed in rogue browser add-ons, specifically Chrome extensions
Steals passwords, promotes content on other networks, inserts ads or popups on legitimate pages
Attack Vector: Lured via email or Facebook Messenger spam
Indicators of Compromise: Sudden rise in Faceliker detections reported by McAfee in Q2 2017
Faceliker accounted for 8.9% of 52 million new malware samples detected in Q2 2017
